fixes.fix: Explained "What do you know about Air commodore (Air Cdre or Air Cmde)?"
fixes.text: VERDICT: Air commodore is an air officer rank originating from the Royal Air Force. WHY: It sits immediately senior to group captain and immediately subordinate to air vice-marshal. TRAPS: Do not confuse it with group captain (subordinate) or air vice-marshal (senior). HOOK: Think of it as the bridge between group captain and air vice-marshal. Exam-day trap: Verify the exact rank hierarchy if options swap adjacent ranks.

fixes.fix: Explained "The equivalent rank in the Women's Auxiliary Air Force, Women's Royal Air Force (until ___"
fixes.text: VERDICT: 1968. WHY: The Women's Royal Air Force (WRAF) ceased to exist in 1968 when it merged into the regular RAF, ending its distinct rank structure. TRAPS: Confusing this with the Princess Mary's RAF Nursing Service, which continued until 1980, or assuming the WAAF/WRAF ranks remained separate post-1968. HOOK: Remember 1968 as the 'WRAF wipeout' year; examiners love testing the specific end-date of auxiliary services rather than general RAF history.

fixes.fix: Explained "In official _____ usage, the rank title was commodore de l'air"
fixes.text: 1) VERDICT: The answer is Canadian French. 2) WHY: In official Canadian French usage, the rank title was commodore de l'air. This reflects the bilingual nature of Canadian defence terminology, where French ranks are standardized for official use. 3) TRAPS: Do not confuse this with British or American French usage, which do not employ this specific rank title in official contexts. The term is unique to Canadian institutional language. 4) HOOK: Remember 'commodore de l'air' as a distinctly Canadia
